study type: Retrospective cohort study (nationwide population-based register study)
exposure: Spine fusion surgery for other reasons
cohort: The study included all fertile-aged women in Finland (1998-2018) who had undergone spine fracture or spine fusion surgery, compared to women without such prior conditions.
finding: The incidence of fusion surgery for other reasons increased by 156% in fertile-aged women, and women with preceding spine fracture or fusion surgery had higher rates of caesarean section and neonates requiring intensive care.
mod_finding: The rate of caesarean section was higher in women with preceding spine fracture or fusion surgery, but the study suggests that vaginal delivery after spine fractures is possible and safe for both mother and neonate.
